features.description: Unconditional `jmp JUMP_ADDR_n` instructions repeatedly route separate basic blocks to a shared in-function continuation or exit, often with a `nop` immediately after the jump.
A call is preceded by loading its second argument into `rsi` and then its first argument into `rdi`, with the two register moves directly adjacent to the call.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
Repeated unrolled processing of adjacent fields through an RAX-based pointer, using fixed-offset operands such as `[rax+CONST]` in `lea` and memory instructions, often alongside bounds checks.
The SysV fifth-argument register `r8` is repeatedly populated from an incoming argument or memory, then carried through register or stack moves for later calls and data accesses.
Dense multiway control flow in which conditional branches and direct `jmp` instructions route separate arms to shared local basic blocks, represented by repeated `JUMP_ADDR_n` destinations.
NO CLEAR PATTERN

A recurring signed half-difference pattern: subtract two bounds or pointers, arithmetic-shift the result right by a constant (`sar reg, CONST`), then use the halved difference in address or size calculations, sometimes with conditional moves for sign handling.
Repeated sign-preserving right shifts of computed values using `sar` on integer registers and `psrad` on SIMD lanes, often before sign extension or packing.
Repeated AVX `vmovdqa` transfers between 128-bit XMM registers and memory, often spilling to or reloading from stack slots around SIMD operations.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
A bounds-checked switch dispatch loads a signed relative offset from an index-scaled jump table, adds the table base, and jumps indirectly through the resulting register.
A recurring entry stub loads an absolute `ds:xxx` operand into `rax` or `eax` and immediately executes `ud2`, typically before `endbr64` and the function prologue.
Repeated `lea reg, off_xxx` instructions materialize addresses of statically located objects, often for storage or use as call arguments.
The code repeatedly accesses 64-bit array or table elements through scaled-index operands such as `[base+index*8+disp]`, often after sign-extending a 32-bit index with `movsxd`.
Integer counters or indices are repeatedly advanced or backed up with `inc` and `dec` as part of arithmetic and memory-access sequences.
The code repeatedly extracts and packs narrow binary fields, using 8- and 16-bit register aliases with shifts, rotates, masks, and zero-extension around subword memory accesses.
A dynamic stack-allocation pattern computes and masks an allocation size, subtracts it from `rsp`, and probes the newly allocated stack with memory touches such as `or [rsp+...], CONST`.
The code uses memory-operand `xchg` instructions to swap a register with a value at a memory location, such as `cs:xxx` or a base-register-plus-offset address.
Packed floating-point SIMD arithmetic uses XMM registers, with instructions such as `mulps`/`addps` or `mulpd`/`addpd` interleaved with vector moves and shuffles in array-processing loops.
A counted data-processing loop increments a stack-resident index by a constant, compares it with a bound, and closes with a `jb` or `jl` back-edge.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN

A 64-bit unsigned-to-floating-point conversion tests the sign bit with `test`/`js`, then handles the high-bit case with `shr`, `and`, and `or`, converts the adjusted value using `cvtsi2ss` or `cvtsi2sd`, and doubles it with `addss` or `addsd`.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code repeatedly uses unsigned `div` with a register or memory divisor, often zeroing `EDX`/`RDX` first and then using the quotient in `EAX`/`RAX` or remainder in `EDX`/`RDX`.
The code repeatedly performs signed integer division by sign-extending RAX with `cqo` and then using `idiv` with a register operand.

A recurring bounds-check idiom compares two register-held sizes, selects the unsigned smaller with `cmp` and `cmovbe`, tests it for zero, then subtracts the bounds and branches on signed thresholds such as `jg` and `jl`.
Legacy SSE/XMM vector data-processing, with packed unpack/pack, shuffle, conversion, and arithmetic instructions such as `punpck*`, `pack*`, `pshufd`, and `mulps`.
A recurring pattern is numerical SSE work in XMM registers, with integer-to-float conversions such as `cvtsi2ss` and `cvtsd2ss` feeding scalar floating-point arithmetic.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN

Local code-label and function addresses recur as operands: they are materialized with `lea` or `mov`, passed through registers and stack slots, stored in objects, and compared against register values.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
A frame-relative stack store uses a register as a dynamic index, as in `mov [rsp+rax+CONST+var_xxx], reg` or `mov [rbp+rax+var_xxx], reg`, often after loading that index from a field.
Repeated loops that transform packed data by extracting and combining bit fields with shifts and masks, using indexed memory loads and stores.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
A repeated wide-integer right-shift idiom uses `shrd` to combine a low/high register pair, commonly followed by `shr` on the high half.

Repeated multiword integer arithmetic keeps values in low/high register halves and uses `shrd`/`shr` with `sbb`/`adc` to shift and propagate carry or borrow across the halves, followed by flag-conditioned branches.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code uses statically based lookup tables, loading register-indexed byte values—often with `movzx`—and combining them in arithmetic or byte-processing loops.

Repeated pointer-table lookups load an array base from an object field, access 8-byte entries with scaled-index operands such as `[rax+index*8]`, then dereference the selected entry to read or update its fields.
The function begins with an `ud2` trap instruction, often followed by `endbr64` or saved-register pushes.
Repeated packed-SIMD lane reshaping with XMM/YMM/ZMM registers, using unpack, shuffle, and pack instructions interleaved with vector arithmetic.

The code dynamically adjusts `rsp` by a computed size, probing the newly allocated stack with page-sized `sub rsp, CONST` steps and memory writes such as `or [rsp+CONST+var_xxx], CONST`, with conditional branches controlling the probes.
Signed-condition conditional moves such as `cmovns`, `cmovg`, and `cmovle` select values after arithmetic or comparisons, implementing branchless sign or bound selection.

A recurring SSE2 floating-point rounding sequence compares a `double` with `ucomisd`, truncates it to an integer with `cvttsd2si`, then corrects the result using `cmpnlesd` and packed mask/select operations.
A recurring array-loop bounds check compares an index or stride-derived value with a limit and uses an unsigned `jb JUMP_ADDR_n` branch to continue the loop.

A vectorized packed-pixel processing loop widens bytes with `punpckhbw`/`punpcklbw`, applies fixed-point packed-word arithmetic such as `paddw` and `pmulhw`, then packs and interleaves the results for vector stores with a scalar tail.
Scalar SSE floating-point comparisons, commonly using COMISD after CVTSS2SD promotion, set flags that drive conditional jumps.

A sign-extended element count is combined with an index and used in a scale-8 `lea` with a fixed displacement to form a pointer from a container base, often just before the function restores registers and returns.
A repeated 128-bit right-shift idiom uses `shrd` to combine the low and high 64-bit registers with an immediate count, paired with `shr` of the high register by the same count.

The functions commonly perform contiguous memory-range copies or relocations using unaligned XMM loads and stores (`movdqu`/`vmovdqu` and `movups`/`vmovups`), with pointer-advancing loops and scalar cleanup.

Repeated SSE-style widening and interleaving of packed bytes in XMM registers with `punpcklbw` and `punpckhbw`, followed by word/dword unpacking and packed arithmetic.
Scalar single-precision values are widened with `cvtss2sd` into XMM registers for double-precision processing, sometimes followed by `cvtsd2ss` to narrow them back.
Repeated C++ virtual-dispatch checks dereference an object’s vptr and method slot, compare the slot with known function addresses and null, then branch around an indirect call.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code contains SSE/XMM packed-integer processing that compares byte or word lanes and blends results with `pand`/`pandn`/`por`, often followed by `punpck` or `pack` lane rearrangement.

The code performs XMM-based packed-data transformations, combining `pand` masks and `psrlw` lane shifts with byte unpacking or packing instructions such as `punpcklbw`, `punpckhbw`, and `packuswb`.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
At call sites, a pointer to a stack-resident temporary or object is set up in `rdi`—often with `lea rax, [rbp/rsp+...]` followed by `mov rdi, rax`—and passed as the first argument.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code repeatedly handles byte- and word-sized values in subregisters, transforming them with shifts or rotates and checking their ranges with immediate comparisons followed by conditional jumps.
The code frequently loads `ECX` with a fixed count, sets up `RSI`/`RDI` as buffer pointers, and executes a `REP`-prefixed string instruction.
The code repeatedly loads 128-bit constant-pool values (`cs:xxx`) into XMM registers with `movdqa`, then uses those vectors in packed SIMD operations or `movups` stores.
Out-of-line `endbr64` blocks preserve `rax` in a callee-saved register, pass a saved object or stack address in `rdi` to a `callfunc_xxx`, and continue through a jump or follow-up call.
A callee-saved `r15` is loaded with an argument or computed address, then used as a live pointer or index for repeated memory accesses and loop or bounds checks.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
Repeated conditional branches and direct `jmp` instructions converge on shared labeled basic blocks, often serving as join points after repeated case or loop paths.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code computes runtime-sized stack buffers with shifts and alignment masks, subtracts the resulting size from `rsp`, and probes the newly allocated stack region with a memory access.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
A condition is materialized as a full-width boolean with `setcc al` followed by `movzx eax, al`, often then tested with `test eax, eax` to steer a conditional branch.
The function uses `rbp` as a stable frame base, reserves local space with `sub rsp, CONST`, and accesses locals through `[rbp+var_xxx]` slots.
A repeated bounds-check idiom: `cmp`/`comiss`/`comisd` sets flags, then `jle`/`jbe` branches on the less-or-equal condition, often to a guard or exit block.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
SSE double-precision arithmetic is followed by narrowing conversions—such as `cvtsd2ss`, `cvtpd2ps`, and truncating double-to-integer conversions—before results are stored.
The prologue probes large stack allocations by subtracting from `rsp` and touching an `rsp`-relative location with `or [rsp+...], imm`, sometimes stepping toward a saved `r11` boundary in a loop.
Repeated signed bounds tests compare index- or length-like values with `cmp`, then use `jl` and `jg` branches to loop or failure targets.
After `call sub_xxx`, the code loads an object’s first pointer-sized field, checks it for null, compares the value it points to with the call’s return value, and branches before a fallback call.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The functions repeatedly compute scalar floating-point expressions in XMM registers, interleaving `subss`/`subsd` with `mulss`/`mulsd` and `addss`/`addsd`.
The code uses `bsr` to find an integer’s highest set bit, often after OR-ing in a constant and then using the resulting bit index in shifts or arithmetic.

The code frequently applies immediate-count `ROL` instructions to integer values, especially 16-bit registers such as `ax`, `bx`, `cx`, and `dx`, often before storing or using the rotated value in further arithmetic.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
Scalar single-precision SSE arithmetic is followed by `ucomiss` comparisons and `jp` branches that handle unordered results.
An `endbr64; sub rsp, imm` entry commonly spills incoming argument registers into `[rsp+…]` slots and saves the `fs` stack canary before making a call.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The code uses BMI2 bit-manipulation instructions—especially register-count shifts such as `shlx`, `shrx`, and `sarx`—often around `and`/`or` operations and conditional branches.
Repeated array-element accesses use scaled-index memory operands—especially `[base+index*4+disp]` for 32-bit elements—within bounds checks and loop-like control flow.
Scalar SSE floating-point code compares values with `comiss` and uses constant-pool operands in arithmetic, including `xorps` with a memory constant as a sign mask.
The code accesses stack-passed arguments at `[rbp+arg_xxx]` with `mov` instructions, loading them into registers for subsequent use.
NO CLEAR PATTERN
The x86 `bt` instruction tests a bit in one register using another register as the bit index, commonly followed by `jb` or `jnb` to branch on the resulting carry flag.
The feature detects compiler-emitted no-op padding, most often `xchg ax, ax`, sometimes as a multi-byte `nop [rax+rax+CONST]` between ordinary instructions.
Repeated `cpuid` queries load a leaf into EAX, test the returned values with conditional branches, and extract feature bits from ECX or EDX using `shr` and `and`.

Repeated accesses to stack-allocated arrays through register-scaled addresses, typically using `movsxd`-extended indices in `[rsp+index*4/8+...]` loads and stores within loops.
Scalar single-precision floating-point division with `divss`, typically embedded in an SSE arithmetic sequence.
A recurring bounds-check idiom uses `cmp` followed by `sbb`—often `sbb reg,reg` to turn the borrow flag into a mask—before branching or continuing address arithmetic.

A recurring byte-field merge zero-extends two values loaded from memory, masks each with an immediate, ORs them together, and stores the low byte back to a structure field.

Sustained XMM-register SIMD computation, interleaving packed-lane arithmetic such as `addps`/`subps`/`mulps` with lane shuffles and bitwise mask operations such as `xorps`.
A long SSE2 packed-integer pipeline operates on XMM registers with `punpck` interleaves, `pmaddwd` multiply-adds, lane shifts, and `pack` operations before storing the vector results.

A repeated pattern tests an immediate bit in memory with `test [rax+CONST], CONST`, converts the nonzero result using `setnz al` and `movzx eax, al`, then stores the Boolean value in a stack slot.
Repeated integer comparisons are followed by `cmovcc` instructions—especially `cmovle` and `cmovg`—to select or clamp a value without branching.

The code uses immediate-count packed-integer shifts on XMM registers, often alongside word additions, unpacking, masking, and `packuswb` to transform byte and word vectors.

Repeated helper calls are followed by `test al, al` and `cmovz` to select between two addresses loaded with `lea` from `GLOBAL_VAR`.
